arxiv-2202-08670.description: Abstract Recently, the use of synthetic datasets based on game engines has been shown to improve the performance of several tasks in computer vision. However, these datasets are typically only appropriate for the specific domains depicted in computer games, such as urban scenes involving vehicles and people.

arxiv-2203-04851.title: Quasi α \alpha -Firmly Nonexpansive Mappings in Wasserstein Spaces
arxiv-2203-04851.creator: Arian Bërdëllima, Gabriele Steidl
arxiv-2203-04851.description: Abstract This paper introduces the concept of quasi α \alpha -firmly nonexpansive mappings in Wasserstein spaces over ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} and analyzes properties of these mappings. We prove that for quasi α \alpha -firmly nonexpansive mappings satisfying a certain quadratic growth condition, the fixed point iterations converge in the narrow topology.

arxiv-2207-07674.title: The Tarantula Massive Binary Monitoring VI: Characterisation of hidden companions in 51 single-lined O-type binaries
arxiv-2207-07674.creator: T. Shenar, H. Sana, L. Mahy, J. Maíz Apellániz, Paul A. Crowther 4, M. Gromadzki 12, A. Herrero 5,6, N. Langer, P. Marchant, Fabian R. N. Schneider 10,11, K. Sen 7,8, I. Soszyński 12, S. Toonen 1
arxiv-2207-07674.description: Abstract Context. Massive binaries hosting a black hole (OB+BH) represent a critical phase in the production of BH mergers in the context of binary evolution. In spite of this, such systems have so far largely avoided detection. Single-lined spectroscopic (SB1) O-type binaries are ideal objects to search for elusive BH companions.

arxiv-2211-13825.title: MeV Dark Matter with MeV Dark Photons in Abelian Kinetic Mixing Theories
arxiv-2211-13825.creator: Federico Compagnin, Stefano Profumo, Nicolao Fornengo
arxiv-2211-13825.description: Abstract Abstract We consider the cosmology and phenomenology of a dark photon portal to a simple dark sector consisting of a single, light, fermionic dark matter particle species with mass in the MeV range. We entertain three possible kinetic mixing structures of a new Abelian gauge group U(1) {}_{\text{dark}} with the visible sector through U(1) {}_{\text{e.m.

arxiv-2304-07427.title: Exact Probabilities for Three and Four Dice in the Balanced Uniform Model of 3-Sided Dice
arxiv-2304-07427.creator: Kent E. Morrison
arxiv-2304-07427.description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Kent E. Morrison. We determine the exact probabilities of the different isomorphism classes of tournaments that result from random sets of three and four independent dice drawn from the balanced uniform model of 3 3 -sided dice. Background and Results

By now it is well-recognized that various models of generalized dice exhibit surprisingly high rates of intransitivity for randomly chosen dice.

arxiv-2304-13567.title: Technical Report: Impact of Position Bias on Language Models in Token Classification CCS: Computing methodologies Information extraction CCS: Computing methodologies Neural networks
arxiv-2304-13567.creator: Mehdi Ben Amor, Michael Granitzer, Jelena Mitrovic
arxiv-2304-13567.description: Abstract . Language Models (LMs) have shown state-of-the-art performance in Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks. Downstream tasks such as Named Entity Recognition (NER) or Part-of-Speech (POS) tagging are known to suffer from data imbalance issues, particularly regarding the ratio of positive to negative examples and class disparities.

arxiv-2501-19012.title: Importing Phantoms: Measuring LLM Package Hallucination Vulnerabilities
arxiv-2501-19012.creator: Arjun Krishna, Erick Galinkin, Leon Derczynski, Jeffrey Martin
arxiv-2501-19012.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have become an essential tool in the programmer’s toolkit, but their tendency to hallucinate code can be used by malicious actors to introduce vulnerabilities to broad swathes of the software supply chain. In this work, we analyze package hallucination behaviour in LLMs across popular programming languages examining both existing package references and fictional dependencies.

arxiv-2512-12996.title: The interplay of magnetic order with the electronic scattering and crystal-field effects in a metallic ferromagnet
arxiv-2512-12996.creator: Payel Shee, 1 Tanaya Halder, 1 Chia-Jung Yang, 2 Nainish Tickoo, 1 Ratiranjan Samal, 1 Ruta Kulkarni, 3 Shishir K. Pandey, 4,5 Vikas Kashid, 6,7 Ashis K. Nandy, 1 Arumugam Thamizhavel, 3 Anamitra Mukherjee, 1 and Shovon Pal 1
arxiv-2512-12996.description: Abstract The interplay between magnetic order, charge dynamics, and crystal field excitations underpins the emergent ground states of rare-earth intermetallics. Using time-domain terahertz spectroscopy, we probe this coupling in PrSi , a metallic ferromagnet. The optical response exhibits pronounced Drude-Smith behavior over a broad temperature range, indicating persistent carrier scattering.

arxiv-2601-18377.title: Socioeconomic Determinants of the COVID-19 Infodemics
arxiv-2601-18377.creator: Anna Bertani, Alessandro Cortese, Federico Pilati, Pierluigi Sacco, Riccardo Gallotti
arxiv-2601-18377.description: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic has been accompanied by an “infodemic” of misinformation that impedes effective public health responses. This study examines relationships between socioeconomic factors and infodemic risk patterns across 37 OECD countries using Twitter data from 2020-2022. Employing dimensionality reduction techniques on 20 socioeconomic indicators, we identify complex correlations with infodemic measures that evolve throughout the pandemic.

pmc-11543174.title: Deficiency of adenosine deaminase 2 (DADA2) presented with bilateral renal subcapsular hematoma: a case report and literature review
pmc-11543174.creator: Majd Al-Ghoul, Jillan Yazbak, Israa Rummanneh, Aseel Abuhammad, Ali H Khalilia, Adnan A M Wahdan
pmc-11543174.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Introduction and importance:Adenosine deaminase 2 (DADA2) deficiency is a monogenic autoinflammatory disease caused by biallelic mutations in the ADA2 gene. Small- and medium-sized vessels may be involved and can cause various clinical symptoms, including features resembling polyarteritis nodosa (PAN).

pmc-11712321.title: Supporting everyday cognition: Home Technology Tours with people living with dementia
pmc-11712321.creator: Arlene Astell, Hira Awan, Danielle Pearson
pmc-11712321.description: BackgroundCurrent off‐the‐shelf technologies contain functionality which can support everyday cognition, such as storing telephone numbers and calendar reminders. These functions can benefit everyone, including people living with dementia. However, knowledge is limited about people living with dementia acquiring and using existing technologies and whether or how they are utilizing these functions.

pmc-12358045.title: The association of organophosphate flame retardants (OPFRs) exposure on omega-3 fatty acids metabolism: evidence derived from the United States general population
pmc-12358045.creator: Ting-Hsuan Hsu, Hsiu-Yung Pan, Kai-Fan Tsai, Chia-Te Kung, Wan-Ting Huang, Huey-Ling You, Shau-Hsuan Li, Chin-Chou Wang, Wen-Chin Lee, Fu-Jen Cheng
pmc-12358045.description: This study investigated the association between exposure to organophosphate flame retardants (OPFRs) and serum omega-3 fatty acid levels in the general U.S. population, using data from 1,350 adults in the 2011–2014 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). OPFRs are widely used in consumer and industrial products, and emerging evidence has linked them to disruptions in lipid metabolism.

pmc-12402087.title: [18F]FDG PET metabolic patterns of the rapid-acting antidepressant effects of NLX-101, a 5-HT1A receptor biased agonist
pmc-12402087.creator: Sarah Chaib, Elise Levigoureux, Sandrine Bouvard, Caroline Bouillot, Benjamin Vidal, Anthony Fourier, Adrian Newman-Tancredi, Luc Zimmer
pmc-12402087.description: Rapid-acting antidepressants (RAADs) such as ketamine are currently under development. The aim of this study is to characterize the neural circuits affected by ketamine and NLX-101, a selective 5-HT1A receptor biased agonist which has shown promising effects, by using [18F]FDG PET imaging in rats that had received chronic administration of corticosterone (CORT), a model of anxiety-depression.

pmc-12428951.title: Autonomic Dysfunction in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS): Findings from the Multi-Site Clinical Assessment of ME/CFS (MCAM) Study in the USA
pmc-12428951.creator: Anindita Issa, Jin-Mann S Lin, Yang Chen, Jacob Attell, Dana Brimmer, Jeanne Bertolli, Benjamin H Natelson, Charles W Lapp, Richard N Podell, Andreas M Kogelnik, Nancy G Klimas, Daniel L Peterson, Lucinda Bateman, Elizabeth R Unger, Svetlana Blitshteyn
pmc-12428951.description: Background/Objectives: Symptoms of autonomic dysfunction are common in infection-associated chronic conditions and illnesses (IACCIs), including myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS). This study aimed to evaluate autonomic symptoms and their impact on ME/CFS illness severity. Methods: Data came from a multi-site study conducted in seven ME/CFS specialty clinics during 2012–2020.

pmc-12624346.title: Current Trends in Antibiotic Resistance Patterns of Pathogens in Urinary Tract Infections in Children in Karaganda, Kazakhstan
pmc-12624346.creator: Shynar Yeleupayeva, Aigul Dinmukhamedova, Roman Aizman, Zhanat Mukataeva, Bibenur Baidalinova, Saule Bazarbaeva, Muhametkali Zhakupov, Zhanar Rakhimzhanova, Aisulu Kuzenbayeva
pmc-12624346.description: Background: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are common in children and result in frequent hospitalization, creating a social and economic burden for parents and the healthcare system. This study analyzes the patterns of antibiotic resistance of dominant uropathogens and assesses the impact of patient age and sex on these patterns.

pmc-13181466.title: Cost-effectiveness and evidence gaps of advanced technologies in lumbar spine surgery: a scoping review
pmc-13181466.creator: Andrea Fabregas, Gonzalo F. Del Rio Montesinos, Andrea Vazquez, Nelson I. Molina Lara, David Vázquez Rodríguez, Lancelot Benn
pmc-13181466.description: BackgroundRobotic guidance, augmented reality (AR), and emerging artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are increasingly integrated into lumbar spine surgery. While improvements in technical accuracy and perioperative metrics have been widely reported, the economic value and feasibility of adopting these technologies remain uncertain.

pmc-13224358.title: Segmentation regularized training for multi-domain deep learning registration applied to magnetic resonance-guided prostate cancer radiotherapy
pmc-13224358.creator: Sudharsan Madhavan, Chengcheng Gui, Lando Bosma, Josiah Simeth, Jue Jiang, Nicolas Côté, Nima Hassan Rezaeian, Himanshu Nagar, Victoria Brennan, Neelam Tyagi, Harini Veeraraghavan
pmc-13224358.description: Graphical abstractUnlabelled Image Introduction Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) guided adaptive radiotherapy (MRgART) combines an onboard MR imager with a linear accelerator, enabling daily treatment adaptation through superior soft-tissue contrast [1], [2]. Daily adaptation requires fast, accurate organ of interest segmentation, commonly achieved through deformable image registration (DIR) for contour propagation [3], [4], [5].

pmc-13258775.title: Association between Dietary Behavior and Mental Health in Adolescents from Multicultural and Non-Multicultural Families in Korea
pmc-13258775.creator: Jeong-Hwa Choi, Young-Ran Heo
pmc-13258775.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objectives: The growing population of multicultural adolescents (MCAs) has become a vital focus for national health policy. Despite their increasing numbers, MCAs often encounter unique socioeconomic challenges and dietary issues that may heighten mental health vulnerabilities. This study aimed to assess the dietary behaviors of MCA and non-MCA and to explore the association between these behaviors and mental health outcomes, specifically generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) and severity of suicidal behavior.

pmc-13453325.title: When Steroids Backfire: A Case of Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State, Pneumocystis Pneumonia, and Cauda Equina Syndrome
pmc-13453325.creator: Bryson T Grondel, Neel Patel, Chris Talone, Nathalie Vanderrijst
pmc-13453325.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Corticosteroids are potent anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive agents frequently used in short courses for various conditions. However, prolonged or inappropriate use can lead to severe complications, including immunosuppression, metabolic derangements, and delayed diagnosis of underlying disease. Cauda equina syndrome is a neurosurgical emergency that can be masked by corticosteroid therapy, while chronic use also predisposes to opportunistic infections such as Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.

uslaw-usc-t15-s4910.title: 15 U.S.C. § 4910 — Nonduplication
uslaw-usc-t15-s4910.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t15-s4910.description: United States Code, Title 15 (Commerce And Trade); Chapter 75 (National Trade Data Bank). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Secretary shall ensure that information systems created or developed pursuant to this chapter do not unnecessarily duplicate information systems available from other Federal agencies or from the private sector.
